segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: After the wife of the chief minister invited Yusuf to zina, to fornication, and after Yusuf said that he would not do it, he then explained why: “Indeed, my lord has treated me well.”
According to one view, he said: Allah has treated me well, so I do not want to do it. According to another view, he said: this master of mine has treated me well,
he received me into his house, so how could I do that? And he said: “The wrongdoer will never succeed.” The wrongdoer will not succeed, the one who repays good with evil.
When Yusuf saw that nothing worked with this woman, neither advice nor anything else, he ran toward the door, to get out of the palace.

And she ran after him, as the Qur'an informs us about it, saying: “وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِنْ دُبُرٍ” – so, it says, Yusuf ran, and she after him, to stop him, to stop him from getting out.

And, it says, she tore his shirt from the back, that is, from behind. As she tried to grab him, to stop him, she tore his shirt. “وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَى الْبَابِ” – and, it says, they met this husband of hers: as the man was returning home, he came upon them, they met him. And, dear brothers, how corrupt – a'udhu billah (I seek refuge in Allah) – the woman was: now she puts herself in the position of the victim.
And she says to her husband, she says: “O my husband, what is the punishment for one who intends evil for your family, who wants to commit fornication with your wife…”
She immediately accused him of being the one who wanted to commit fornication with her, and not the other way around. “…except that he be thrown into prison or punished with a severe punishment.”
Or that he be punished – that is, you have, my husband, two choices: either throw him into prison, or punish him with a severe punishment.

What happens next? Yusuf answers immediately. Here, dear brothers, is a lesson for us: when someone accuses us, we should cut it off at once, not beat around the bush: “Well, look, well, like this, well, like that, listen, it didn't happen that way.”
What does Yusuf say? He says, Yusuf, alayhis-salam, says: “No, no, no,” he says, “she,” he says, “asked me to commit fornication with her; it wasn't me, I didn't want that.” He cut it off at once.
وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا
segmenti.prevod: “…and a witness from her own family testified…” (Yusuf 12:26)

segmenti.tekst: Then a witness from her family testified – not from his family, but from her family, and a relative, in sha Allah, will not lie against a relative. So there was wisdom in this witness being from her family. The mufassirun (Qur'an commentators) say that this witness was her paternal cousin; some say he was her maternal cousin; some say he was a friend of this chief minister, his best friend, and her relative.

Some of the mufassirun even say that it was a small infant who spoke, but that doesn't matter; what matters is that he testified. What was his testimony, in what way? “In kana qamisuhu qudda min qubulin fa sadaqat wa huwa min al-kadhibin” – he said: if the shirt is torn from the front, then she spoke the truth

and he lied, because if it is torn from the front, then she was defending herself, defending herself from him. “وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ” – and if the shirt is torn from behind, then, he said, she is lying and he is telling the truth. See how clever this witness was.
He immediately gave them the solution: if the shirt is torn from the front, then, that is, he is the liar, because she was trying to defend herself from him.
If it is from behind, then she is lying, because she tried to stop him from getting out.
فَلَمَّا رَأَىٰ قَمِيصَهُ قُدَّ مِنْ دُبُرٍ قَالَ إِنَّهُ مِنْ كَيْدِكُنَّ ۖ إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌ
segmenti.prevod: “So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, ‘Indeed, this is of your plotting; indeed, your plotting is great.’” (Yusuf 12:28)

segmenti.tekst: So when he saw that the shirt was torn, ripped from behind: “This is,” he said, “one of your schemes,” said this husband. “This is,” he said, “one of your schemes” – and a man knows his wife best – “indeed,” he said, “your schemes” – he means women here – “indeed,” he said, “your schemes are great.” Now there is an interesting detail here, dear brothers.

Many people today use these words of this man against women, and they say, that is, they prove with this verse, that women are the ones who scheme, and so on, that their schemes are great, and so on. So, let us be clear: this is no proof at all. These are the words of this chief minister; these are neither the words of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), nor the words of the Messenger of Allah. These are only his words, which does not mean they are correct.
The second thing is: a person must by no means think that those Muslim women who are pious are corrupt, that they scheme, and so on. Here it is about a disbelieving woman.

That is, this woman was a disbeliever, she was not a believer. And believing women are, with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, pure and good and do not scheme. Here what is meant is this disbelieving woman. So a person should immediately, when someone [unclear] argues to him against women, stop him and say: “No, no, no, brother, this is… you'd better look into it a bit, you'd better read a bit more,” and so on, and so on, and so forth. What does he do, that is, what happens next, when this husband of hers saw it? Also an interesting situation, dear brothers.

He said: “Yusuf, leave this alone, don't,” he said, “talk about this, so that it doesn't spread, this is a great disgrace what she did. Wastaghfiri li dhanbiki – my wife,” he said, “seek forgiveness from the Lord.

Innaki kunti min al-khati'in – indeed you are,” he said, “among those who have sinned. Indeed you are among those who have sinned, so seek forgiveness from your Lord.” It is interesting, dear brothers, that this man merely turned around and said: “Yusufu a'rid 'an hadha.”
“Yusuf,” he said, “turn away from this, leave this alone.” He did not show, dear brothers, any protective jealousy, he did not show any protective jealousy.

One of the mufassirun, the commentators of the Qur'an, the well-known al-Qurtubi – he lived in Spain; many know his “Al-Jami' li Ahkam al-Qur'an”. He lived in Spain, and after Spain fell, he moved to Egypt.

And he saw the difference in attitude toward women between those who lived in Spain and those who lived in Egypt. And he mentions there, he says: “We,” he says, “those who lived in Spain, are very protective,” because at that time Spain was the center of Islamic civilization.

“So we,” he says, “guarded our wives. Our wives were nicely covered, they did not go out where they should not go, and so on, and so forth. But when I came to Egypt, I came across something completely the opposite.

I saw,” he says, “that people are not very protective of their wives.” So he says: no wonder this man reacted in this way, that is, without jealousy, but only said: “Yusuf, leave this alone,” and that was it, and the man left.

He did not react. Perhaps someone else would have reacted differently. Perhaps someone would have killed his wife, struck her, and so on. So, he had no reaction at all. After this, my dear brothers, stories began to spread through Egypt, and we will, in sha Allahu ta'ala, speak about that tomorrow.
That is all, in sha Allah, for today. May Allah grant you every good and give you long life in khayr (goodness). As-salamu alaykum.
